references.text: Parallel text mentioning both the Feast of Weeks (firstfruits of wheat) and the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year.
Detailed regulations for the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), celebrated seven weeks after Passover with the firstfruits of wheat.
Sacrificial regulations for the Day of Firstfruits, also called the Feast of Weeks.
Instructions for celebrating the Feast of Weeks, seven weeks from the beginning of the grain harvest.
Instructions for the Feast of Tabernacles (Feast of Ingathering) at the end of the year.
Detailed regulations for the Feast of Tabernacles, which corresponds to the Feast of Ingathering mentioned in the verse.
Pentecost (Greek: Pentekoste) in the New Testament is the fulfillment of the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), when the Holy Spirit was poured out.
Paul wished to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost, showing that the Feast of Weeks was still celebrated in New Testament times.
Complementary text specifying ritual requirements (sacrifices and rest) for the Feast of Weeks mentioned in the source verse.
Highlights ritual practice: The source verse defines the feast, while this verse describes the actual offering of the firstfruits.
Expands the definition of 'the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year' with specific dates and duration.
Confirms the details of 'the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year' with specific rules for holy assembly and rest.
